anchors.why: Without a trusted grid, the folded text tail is all there is; a trailing caret there also belongs to trust, sign-in and model menus, which the named scan rules out.

rules.why: The bottom four rows at an idle composer. The hint row decides: the caret stays painted through a turn and behind the /model picker, but the hint reads `esc to cancel` mid-turn and in the palette, and the picker covers it. The caret row may carry the edit mode (`> Accept-edits mode: ...`), but never other text: menus prefix their highlighted row with `> ` too. Quiet because a submit repaints the composer for a moment mid-turn.

agy 1.4 lists running background tasks (`● [14:12:56] sleep 900 running`) under the composer, closed by another rule above the hint row, so the composer is no longer in the bottom four rows. The hint row still decides as in composer_ready: a turn's own foreground command is listed the same way, but the hint then reads `esc to cancel`. One task row is required so the rule cannot collapse onto composer_ready's rows; more than six tasks reads as not shown.

A custom statusLine replaces the hint row, so `esc to cancel` never shows; agy 1.5.2 then marks a turn only with a braille spinner row above the composer. Status rows may not hold a rule run, a hint, or agy's own `[mode · ]model · effort` footer, which drops its hint while the composer holds a draft. Pickers between the composer and status rows break the run. A custom row shaped like that footer holds; a mode-shaped draft above a custom statusLine still reads idle.
A readable screen that is not the idle composer may be a picker, dialog or busy turn, which a name-only title or a quiet process cannot see.
